title: Greatest Common Divisor of Strings
description:
A nonempty string base divides a string if repeating base some positive whole number of times produces that string exactly. Given str1 and str2, return the longest string that divides both, or "" if none exists.

Two strings can share a prefix without sharing a repeating unit. If they do have a common unit, their lengths constrain its size; checking how the strings join in both orders reveals whether the same pattern underlies both.

Example 1:

Input: str1 = "ABCABC", str2 = "ABC"
Output: "ABC"

Example 2:

Input: str1 = "ABABAB", str2 = "ABAB"
Output: "AB"

Example 3:

Input: str1 = "LEET", str2 = "CODE"
Output: ""

Constraints:

  • 1 <= str1.length, str2.length <= 1,000
  • Both strings consist only of uppercase English letters.

exampleTestCases.explanation: ABC repeats twice in the first string and once in the second.
AB is the longest unit whose repetitions form both strings.
No nonempty block repeats to form both strings.
